subject: Business Models
title: Automotive Dealerships
description: Learn Automotive Dealerships in one minute.

hook.text: In 49 US states, you can't buy a car directly from the manufacturer. You must go through a franchised dealer.

buildup.text: Dealer franchise laws were created in the 1950s to protect small dealers from manufacturer power.

discovery.text: Dealerships make most profit from service, financing, and add-ons—not the car sale itself.

twist.text: Tesla sells direct-to-consumer, bypassing dealers. Dealer associations have sued Tesla in multiple states.

climax.text: Auto franchising shows how franchise laws, once protective, can become barriers to innovation.

punchline.text: Can't buy direct in 49 states. Franchise law protects dealers, not buyers.

quiz.question: Where do auto dealerships make most of their profit?

details.summary: Automotive dealerships operate as franchises of car manufacturers, holding exclusive territorial rights to sell and service specific brands. Dealer franchise laws in most US states prohibit manufacturers from selling directly to consumers, creating a legally protected intermediary layer.
details.whyItMatters: Auto dealerships are the largest franchise category by revenue. The legal prohibition on direct manufacturer sales, which Tesla has fought.
takeaways: Dealer franchise laws prohibit most manufacturers from selling directly to consumers
Dealerships hold exclusive territorial rights to sell and service specific car brands
Tesla's direct sales model challenges the legally protected dealership franchise system

faq.question: Why can't car manufacturers sell directly to consumers in most states?
faq.answer: State dealer franchise laws, lobbied for by the National Automobile Dealers Association, prohibit or restrict direct manufacturer-to-consumer sales. These laws were originally meant to protect dealers from manufacturer abuse but now primarily protect the dealership business model from disruption.

faq.question: How has Tesla challenged the traditional dealership model?
faq.answer: Tesla sells directly through company-owned stores and online, arguing new EV manufacturers should not be bound by laws designed for legacy dealer relationships. This has led to state-by-state legal battles, with some states allowing Tesla direct sales and others requiring dealer intermediaries.
